oneLineDefinition: A discipline focused on the systematic study of laws, legal systems, rights, and the application of legal principles to resolve disputes and guide behavior.
overview: Law in Vietnam involves mastering the Vietnamese legal system — civil law, criminal law, commercial law, administrative law, and increasingly international law. It is one of the most reading-intensive majors: students must memorize legal codes, analyze cases, and construct precise legal arguments. Unlike in some countries, Law graduates who wish to become licensed lawyers must complete additional professional training and satisfy legal practice requirements under current regulations.
toolsAndTechnologies: Research databases (for academic and international law)
typicalProjects: Draft a commercial contract for a business transaction
Analyze a civil dispute case and write a legal opinion
Research a legal issue and produce a memorandum
Moot court: argue a case before a simulated tribunal
Review and advise on an employment contract for compliance
requiredSkills: Reading stamina — law involves reading enormous volumes of legislation and cases
Memory for legal codes, articles, and precedents
Written clarity — legal documents must be unambiguous
suitableFor: Students who enjoy reading, argumentation, and logical reasoning
Those interested in justice, rights, and governance
Students who are methodical, precise, and comfortable with rule-based systems
Those who want a respected profession with long-term career stability
notSuitableFor: Students who dislike reading long documents and memorizing detailed rules
Those who want fast-paced, results-driven work environments
Students who struggle with writing clear, structured arguments
keyTakeaways: Law is a profession, not just a degree — the practical training period after graduation is essential
Specialization matters — generalist lawyers are common but specialists (M&A, IP, labor) command higher fees
English is increasingly important for international commercial law and foreign-invested enterprise work
Career progression is slower than in tech — seniority and trust take time to build
cautionNotes: The Vietnamese legal market is crowded at the junior level — internships at reputable firms during school are critical
Working hours in large law firms or corporate legal departments can be very demanding
Law graduates who do not pursue practical training and bar qualification often end up in non-legal roles
careerPaths: Lawyer / Attorney (after training and bar qualification)
marketDemand: Stable. Corporate legal, M&A, and compliance roles at foreign-invested enterprises are in consistent demand. Public sector legal roles are competitive. General practice is crowded.
salaryOutlook: Junior lawyers at small firms in Vietnam earn 8–15M VND/month. Corporate lawyers at MNC legal departments or large law firms earn 20–50M. Senior lawyers, partners, and in-house counsel at top companies earn significantly more.
futureTrend: Legal tech and AI are automating document review and contract analysis. Lawyers who understand technology and work in high-value areas (M&A, IP, fintech regulation) are better positioned. Demand for compliance specialists is growing with increasing regulatory complexity.
commonMisconceptions: Studying law means becoming a lawyer
Studying law means you will argue cases in court — most lawyers never see a courtroom; they work on contracts, compliance, and advisory
Law graduates automatically become lawyers — you must complete a mandatory training program and pass qualification requirements
Law is only for students who want to defend criminals — criminal law is a small part of a very large field

faq.question: Is law a good choice in Vietnam for career prospects?
faq.answer: Yes, especially for those willing to specialize and intern early. Corporate law, M&A, and compliance at foreign-invested companies offer good pay and growth. The crowded general practice market is harder to break into without a strong network and firm reputation.

faq.question: Do I need to be good at math to study law?
faq.answer: No. Law is primarily reading, argumentation, and writing. Mathematics beyond basic numeracy is not required. The main demands are reading stamina, precision in language, and logical reasoning.

faq.question: Is law mostly memorization?
faq.answer: No. Memorizing legal provisions is important, but the core skill is interpreting and applying laws to specific situations through logical reasoning and argumentation.
